landmarks.name: Brooklyn Borough Hall
landmarks.fact: Brooklyn's city hall from when it was its own city, until 1898.
landmarks.about: Brooklyn Borough Hall is a building in Downtown Brooklyn, New York City. It was designed by architects Calvin Pollard and Gamaliel King in the Greek Revival style, and constructed of Tuckahoe marble under the supervision of superintendent Stephen Haynes.

landmarks.name: Barclays Center
landmarks.fact: Its rusted-steel skin is made of 12,000 weathered panels.
landmarks.about: Barclays Center ( BAR-kleez) is a multi-purpose indoor arena in the New York City borough of Brooklyn in the United States. The arena is home to the New York Liberty of the Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) and the Brooklyn Nets of the National Basketball Association (NBA).

landmarks.name: Jane's Carousel
landmarks.fact: A 1922 carousel restored over 25 years, now in a glass box by the river.
landmarks.about: Jane's Carousel (formerly Idora Park Merry-Go-Round) is a carved wooden 48-horse carousel in Brooklyn, New York City, built in 1922 by the Philadelphia Toboggan Company (PTC) for the Idora Park amusement park in Youngstown, Ohio.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Heights Promenade
landmarks.fact: It sits on top of a highway, with one of the best views of Manhattan.
landmarks.about: The Brooklyn Heights Promenade, also called the Esplanade, is a 1,826-foot-long (557 m) platform and pedestrian walkway cantilevered over the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (Interstate 278) in Brooklyn Heights, Brooklyn, New York City, United States.

landmarks.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard
landmarks.fact: It built the USS Missouri, where World War II ended.
landmarks.about: The Brooklyn Navy Yard (originally known as the New York Navy Yard) is a shipyard and industrial complex in northwest Brooklyn in New York City, New York, U.S. The Navy Yard is located on the East River in Wallabout Bay, a semicircular bend of the river across from Corlears Hook in Manhattan.

landmarks.name: Domino Park
landmarks.fact: Built on the site of a sugar refinery that once made half of America's sugar.
landmarks.about: Domino Park is a 5-acre (2.0 ha) public park in the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. It spans a quarter mile along the East River near the Williamsburg Bridge, at the Domino Sugar Refinery site.

landmarks.name: Fort Greene Park
landmarks.fact: Its 149-foot column honors over 11,000 prisoners who died on British ships.
landmarks.about: Fort Greene Park is a city-owned and -operated park in Fort Greene, Brooklyn. The 30.2-acre (12.2 ha) park was originally named after the fort formerly located there, Fort Putnam, itself was named for Rufus Putnam, George Washington's chief of engineers in the Revolutionary War.

landmarks.name: Grand Army Plaza
landmarks.fact: Its arch honors Union soldiers of the Civil War.
landmarks.about: Grand Army Plaza, originally known as Prospect Park Plaza, is a public plaza that comprises the northern corner and the main entrance of Prospect Park in the New York City borough of Brooklyn.

landmarks.name: Pratt Institute
landmarks.fact: Its campus doubles as a sculpture park with over 70 works.
landmarks.about: Pratt Institute is a private university with its main campus in Brooklyn, New York. It has an additional campus in Manhattan and an extension campus in Utica, New York at the Munson-Williams-Proctor Arts Institute.

landmarks.name: Williamsburg Bridge (Brooklyn)
landmarks.fact: Its towers were the first bridge towers made entirely of steel.
landmarks.about: The Williamsburg Bridge is a suspension bridge across the East River in New York City, connecting the Lower East Side of Manhattan with the Williamsburg neighborhood of Brooklyn. Originally known as the East River Bridge, the Williamsburg Bridge was completed in 1903.

landmarks.name: Gowanus Canal
landmarks.fact: Once one of the most polluted waterways in the US, now a Superfund cleanup.
landmarks.about: The Gowanus Canal (originally known as Gowanus Creek) is a 1.8-mile-long (2.9 km) canal in the New York City borough of Brooklyn, on the westernmost portion of Long Island.

landmarks.name: McCarren Park
landmarks.fact: Its huge 1936 pool sat empty for 28 years before reopening in 2012.
landmarks.about: McCarren Park is a public park in Brooklyn, New York City. It is located on the border of Williamsburg and Greenpoint and is bordered by Nassau Avenue, Bayard Street, Lorimer Street and North 12th Street.

landmarks.name: DUMBO Archway
landmarks.fact: DUMBO stands for Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass.
landmarks.about: Dumbo (or DUMBO, an acronym for Down Under the Manhattan Bridge Overpass) is a neighborhood in the New York City borough of Brooklyn.

targets.name: Juliana's Pizza
targets.fact: Coal-oven pizza from Patsy Grimaldi, a legend of NYC pizza.
targets.about: Juliana's is a pizzeria located in Brooklyn, New York, founded in 2012 by Pasquale "Patsy" Grimaldi and named after his mother. In 2015, it was rated the best pizzeria in the United States on TripAdvisor.
targets.riddle: Visit this Brooklyn spot, founded by a legend and named for his mother, to taste the best slice in the country.

targets.name: Peter Luger Steak House
targets.fact: Serving porterhouse steaks since 1887, and cash-only for decades.
targets.about: Peter Luger Steak House is a steakhouse located in the Williamsburg section of Brooklyn, New York City, with a second location in Great Neck, New York, in the western part of Long Island.
targets.riddle: Bring your paper bills to this Williamsburg institution for a legendary porterhouse that has been served for over a century.

targets.name: Junior's Restaurant
targets.fact: The original home of Junior's famous cheesecake, since 1950.
targets.about: Junior's is a restaurant chain with the original location at 386 Flatbush Avenue Extension at the corner of DeKalb Avenue in Downtown Brooklyn, New York City. Other locations include the Times Square area and the lobby of the Fox Tower in the Foxwoods Resort in  Ledyard, Connecticut.
targets.riddle: Find the corner of Flatbush Avenue Extension and DeKalb Avenue to taste a famous dessert served since 1950.

targets.name: Lucali
targets.fact: A candlelit pizza spot with no phone reservations and long lines.
targets.about: Lucali is a pizzeria founded by Mark Iacono in 2006, located in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, New York City. The pizzeria serves brick oven pizza and calzones.
targets.riddle: Wait in a long line for brick oven pies or calzones at this candlelit Carroll Gardens spot that takes no reservations.

targets.name: Sahadi's
targets.fact: A Middle Eastern grocery on Atlantic Avenue since 1948.
targets.about: Sahadi's  is a shop in Brooklyn, New York City. The business was established in Manhattan in 1895, and relocated to Brooklyn in 1941.
targets.riddle: Find this Middle Eastern grocery on Atlantic Avenue that moved from Manhattan to Brooklyn long ago.

targets.name: Time Out Market New York
targets.fact: A food hall in a Civil War-era warehouse with a rooftop view.
targets.about: Empire Stores is a former warehouse complex along the waterfront Brooklyn Bridge Park within the neighborhood of Dumbo, Brooklyn, New York City, in the U.S. state of New York.
targets.credit: R.scholz at English Wikipedia CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: Dine in a Civil War-era waterfront warehouse within Dumbo and head to the rooftop for a view of the park.

targets.name: Brooklyn Brewery
targets.fact: Its logo was designed by Milton Glaser, who also made I ♥ NY.
targets.about: Brooklyn Brewery is a brewery in Brooklyn, New York, United States. It was started in 1988 by Steve Hindy and Tom Potter.
targets.riddle: Visit the borough home to the craft taproom whose iconic branding was created by the designer of I ♥ NY.

targets.name: Brooklyn Museum
targets.fact: One of the largest art museums in the US, with 1.5 million works.
targets.about: The Brooklyn Museum is an art museum in the New York City borough of Brooklyn. At 560,000 square feet (52,000 m2), the museum is New York City's second largest and contains an art collection with around 500,000 objects.
targets.riddle: Explore this borough’s vast home to half a million objects, ranking second in size across the entire city.

targets.name: Brooklyn Academy of Music
targets.fact: America's oldest performing arts center still running, since 1861.
targets.about: The Brooklyn Academy of Music (BAM) is a multi-arts center in Brooklyn, New York City. It hosts progressive and avant-garde performances, with theater, dance, music, opera, film programming across multiple nearby venues.
targets.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA CC BY 2.0
targets.riddle: Visit this historic multi-arts center to experience progressive theater, dance, and film in the heart of the borough.

targets.name: New York Transit Museum
targets.fact: It lives inside a real 1936 subway station.
targets.about: The New York Transit Museum (also called the NYC Transit Museum) is a museum that displays historical artifacts of the New York City Subway, bus, and commuter rail systems in the greater New York City metropolitan region.
targets.riddle: Descend into a decommissioned subterranean stop to explore historical artifacts of the city's vast rail and bus networks.

targets.name: Center for Brooklyn History
targets.fact: Holds the borough's archives, from maps to Dodgers memorabilia.
targets.about: The Center for Brooklyn History (CBH, formerly known as the Brooklyn Historical Society) is a museum, library, and educational center founded in 1863 that preserves and encourages the study of Brooklyn's 400-year history.
targets.riddle: Visit this home for archives, maps, and baseball treasures that preserve the storied past of our entire borough.

targets.name: St. Ann's Warehouse
targets.fact: A theater built inside the walls of an 1860s tobacco warehouse.
targets.about: St. Ann's Warehouse is a performing arts organization in Brooklyn, New York City.
targets.riddle: Find this performing arts space hidden within the brick walls of a former tobacco storage building in Brooklyn.

targets.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
targets.fact: Its cherry blossom festival draws huge crowds every spring.
targets.about: Brooklyn Botanic Garden (BBG) is a botanical garden in the borough of Brooklyn in New York City. The botanical garden occupies 52 acres (21 ha) in central Brooklyn, close to Mount Prospect Park, Prospect Park, and the Brooklyn Museum.
targets.riddle: Visit this fifty-two acre floral sanctuary in central borough lands, located right beside the grand museum and famous park.

targets.name: Cobble Hill Park
targets.fact: A tiny neighborhood park saved from becoming a supermarket.
targets.about: Cobble Hill is a neighborhood in the northwestern portion of the New York City borough of Brooklyn.
targets.riddle: Once destined to be a grocery store, this miniature neighborhood green space remains a peaceful refuge in northwestern Brooklyn.

targets.name: Commodore Barry Park
targets.fact: Brooklyn's oldest park, named for the father of the US Navy.
targets.about: Commodore Barry Park is an urban park in the Fort Greene neighborhood of the New York City borough of Brooklyn. The park is operated by the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation.
targets.credit: This photo was taken by participant/team Jim Henderson as part of the Commons:Wi Public domain
targets.riddle: Visit the oldest green space in the borough, dedicated to the man known as the father of the naval fleet.

targets.name: Cadman Plaza Park
targets.fact: Home to Brooklyn's World War II memorial.
targets.about: Cadman Plaza is a park located on the border of the Brooklyn Heights and Downtown Brooklyn neighborhoods in Brooklyn, New York City.
targets.riddle: Find the memorial honoring a global conflict where downtown meets the heights in this borough green space.

targets.name: Williamsburgh Savings Bank Tower
targets.fact: Brooklyn's tallest building for 80 years, with a giant four-sided clock.
targets.about: The Williamsburgh Savings Bank Tower, also known as One Hanson Place, is a skyscraper in the Fort Greene neighborhood of Brooklyn in New York City, New York, U.S.
targets.credit: Gryffindor; cropped by Beyond My Ken (talk) 21:26, 9 October 2012 (UTC) CC BY-SA 3.0
targets.riddle: In Fort Greene stands the tallest structure, watching over the neighborhood with its giant four-sided timepiece.

targets.name: Old Stone House
targets.fact: A rebuilt 1699 farmhouse at the center of the Battle of Brooklyn.
targets.about: The Old Stone House is a house located in the Park Slope neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. It is situated within the J.
targets.riddle: Seek this rebuilt farmhouse in Park Slope that stands at the center of a historic battle.

targets.name: Plymouth Church
targets.fact: A stop on the Underground Railroad; Lincoln worshipped here.
targets.about: Plymouth Church is a Congregational church located at 57 Orange Street, between Henry and Hicks Streets, in the Brooklyn Heights neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York City. The Church House is located at 75 Hicks Street.
targets.riddle: Visit this Brooklyn Heights sanctuary where a president once prayed and freedom seekers found a path to safety.

targets.name: Clock Tower Building
targets.fact: Its glass clock faces frame one of NYC's most famous views.
targets.riddle: Look through these glass faces to frame one of the most famous views in the city.
